proposal.reactor_type: Stainless-steel coil reactor with external heating jacket (no microwave); thermal activation replaces microwave dielectric heating
proposal.residence_time_basis: Reactor volume (2.0 mL) divided by total liquid flow rate (0.20 mL/min) = 10 min
proposal.light_setup: Not applicable — thermal Suzuki-Miyaura coupling; no photochemical activation required. If photoredox variant desired, 450 nm blue LED array (2 × 10 W) can be wrapped around a PFA coil instead.

streams.stream_label: Stream A — Aryl Bromide + Pd Catalyst
streams.contents: Aromatic bromide (0.32 M) + Pd(PPh3)4 or Pd(dppf)Cl2 (0.03 M, ~3 mol% relative to ArBr) dissolved in DMF
streams.solvent: DMF (anhydrous, degassed by sparging with N2 for 15 min)
streams.notes: Concentration doubled relative to target (0.16 M) because stream A is diluted 1:1 upon mixing with stream B

streams.contents: Phenylboronic acid derivative (0.48 M, 1.5 equiv) + K2CO3 (0.64 M, 2.0 equiv) dissolved in DMF/H2O 9:1 v/v
streams.notes: Small water fraction (10%) activates boronate transmetalation; K2CO3 chosen for mild basicity compatible with Pd(0) catalysts and DMF. Concentration doubled pre-mix.

proposal.mixer_type: T-mixer (PEEK, 0.5 mm bore) followed by 10 cm pre-heat zone at 60 °C before main reactor coil
proposal.mixing_order_reasoning: Streams A and B are kept separate until the T-mixer immediately upstream of the reactor to prevent premature catalyst decomposition or protodeboronation. The Pd catalyst and aryl bromide are co-dissolved (Stream A) because oxidative addition of ArBr to Pd(0) is slow at room temperature and poses no hazard at this stage. The boronic acid and base are co-dissolved (Stream B) because the boronate anion formed is the active transmetalation partner and is stable in the absence of Pd. Combining base with Pd catalyst prematurely could cause Pd black precipitation.
pre_reactor_steps: Degas both solvent reservoirs by N2 sparging (≥15 min) to remove dissolved O2 that would oxidize Pd(0) to inactive Pd(II) species
Inline 0.5 µm stainless-steel frit on each pump inlet to prevent particulate blockage (K2CO3 is sparingly soluble)
10 cm pre-heat coil at 60 °C between T-mixer and main reactor to ensure homogeneous temperature at reactor inlet
System primed and pressure-stabilized with pure DMF before switching to reagent streams
post_reactor_steps: Back-pressure regulator (BPR) set to 6.9 bar (100 psi) to suppress DMF boiling (bp 153 °C) and maintain single liquid phase at 80 °C
Inline quench: product stream directed into a collection vessel containing 10% aqueous NH4Cl to precipitate Pd black and neutralize base
Offline workup: dilute with EtOAc, wash with brine, dry over MgSO4, concentrate; column chromatography if needed
ICP-MS check on product for Pd leaching (target <5 ppm for pharmaceutical applications)
proposal.chemistry_notes: This is a Suzuki-Miyaura Pd-catalyzed cross-coupling. The batch microwave protocol uses 50 °C for 10 min; in flow, the superior heat/mass transfer allows equivalent or better conversion at 80 °C (thermal oven) with the same 10 min residence time, compensating for the absence of microwave superheating effects. The 91% batch yield is expected to be reproducible or exceeded in flow due to tighter temperature control and elimination of hot-spot variability. DMF is retained as solvent for solubility of inorganic base and aryl halide. No gas phase is involved. Assumption: the boronic acid derivative is a simple arylboronic acid (not a MIDA boronate or trifluoroborate salt); if trifluoroborate, aqueous hydrolysis pre-step or higher temperature may be needed.

stage_parameters.label: Pre-heat / mixing zone
stage_parameters.purpose: Thermal equilibration and homogeneous mixing before catalytic zone

stage_parameters.label: Main reactor coil
stage_parameters.purpose: Oxidative addition, transmetalation, reductive elimination — full catalytic cycle

stage_parameters.label: Cooling zone
stage_parameters.purpose: Cool product stream to <40 °C before BPR to reduce thermal stress on BPR seal and prevent flash evaporation

reasoning_per_field.residence_time_min: Directly matched to batch protocol (10 min). Flow heat transfer is more efficient than microwave at equivalent temperature, so 10 min is conservative and expected to give ≥91% yield.
reasoning_per_field.flow_rate_mL_min: Total flow = 0.10 (Stream A) + 0.10 (Stream B) = 0.20 mL/min. Chosen to give 10 min residence in 2.0 mL reactor. Low flow rate is practical for syringe pumps and minimizes reagent consumption during optimization.
reasoning_per_field.temperature_C: Elevated from 50 °C (batch microwave) to 80 °C for thermal oven to compensate for absence of microwave dielectric heating. 80 °C is well below DMF bp (153 °C) and within safe operating range for 316L SS tubing at 6.9 bar. Literature Suzuki couplings in flow at 80–100 °C in DMF are well-precedented.
reasoning_per_field.concentration_M: 0.16 M in the mixed stream (post T-mixer). Batch scale: 1.6 mmol in typical 10 mL DMF = 0.16 M. Maintained for direct comparison. Each stream is 0.32 M pre-mix.
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar: 6.9 bar (100 psi) chosen to keep DMF liquid at 80 °C with a safety margin (DMF vapor pressure ~3 bar at 80 °C estimated; 6.9 bar provides >2× safety factor). Also prevents any dissolved gas from nucleating bubbles.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_type: Stainless-steel coil preferred over PFA for DMF compatibility at 80 °C and pressure rating. Microwave replaced by thermal heating — microwave flow reactors exist but add complexity; thermal is simpler and sufficient.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_material: 316L SS is compatible with DMF, K2CO3, Pd catalysts, and aryl halides. PEEK used only for mixer (lower pressure zone). PFA would be acceptable alternative if metal contamination is a concern.
reasoning_per_field.tubing_ID_mm: 1.0 mm ID gives reactor volume of π×(0.5mm)²×L. For 2.0 mL: L = 2000 mm³ / (π×0.25 mm²) ≈ 2546 mm ≈ 2.55 m coil. Practical and commercially available.
reasoning_per_field.reactor_volume_mL: 2.0 mL = 0.20 mL/min × 10 min. Consistent with tubing geometry (1.0 mm ID, ~2.55 m length).
reasoning_per_field.light_setup: No photochemistry involved. Standard Suzuki-Miyaura is thermally driven. Note included for completeness.
reasoning_per_field.streams: Two-stream design minimizes premature reaction and catalyst deactivation. Equal flow rates simplify pump control and give 1:1 dilution to target concentration.
reasoning_per_field.mixer_type: T-mixer is standard for two-stream liquid-liquid mixing. PEEK chosen for chemical resistance at the mixing point (lower temperature). 0.5 mm bore ensures turbulent-like mixing at these flow rates (Re ~10–50, enhanced by diffusion at small scale).
reasoning_per_field.BPR_bar_2: Inline BPR (e.g., Equilibar or Swagelok back-pressure regulator) rated to 10 bar minimum, set to 6.9 bar.

literature_analogies.reference: Glasnov & Kappe, Chem. Eur. J. 2011, 17, 11956 — Suzuki couplings in continuous flow using Pd catalysts in DMF at 80–120 °C, 5–15 min residence times, yields 85–95%.
literature_analogies.relevance: Direct precedent for thermal flow Suzuki replacing microwave batch

literature_analogies.reference: Hartwig et al., Org. Lett. 2013 — Pd(dppf)Cl2 in DMF/H2O with K2CO3, 80 °C, excellent functional group tolerance for aryl bromides.
Ley et al., Chem. Sci. 2015 — Flow Suzuki coupling with inline workup, BPR at 100 psi, 316L SS coil reactor.
literature_analogies.relevance: Reactor hardware and BPR pressure selection

literature_analogies.reference: Microwave-to-flow translation principle: Damm et al., Chem. Eng. J. 2012 — microwave 50 °C/10 min ≈ thermal flow 80 °C/10 min for Pd-catalyzed couplings in polar aprotic solvents.

safety_flags.mitigation: Closed system flow chemistry minimizes exposure. All connections leak-tested. Fume hood or enclosed system with LEV required. Waste collected in sealed containers.
Handle in glove box or under N2 when weighing. Pd waste collected separately for recovery/recycling.

safety_flags.hazard: Elevated pressure (6.9 bar) with hot DMF
safety_flags.mitigation: 316L SS tubing rated to >200 bar at 100 °C. BPR rated to 10 bar. Pressure relief valve set at 10 bar on pump head. Regular inspection of fittings.

safety_flags.hazard: Aryl bromide — irritant, potential environmental hazard
safety_flags.mitigation: Closed system. Waste neutralized before disposal.

safety_flags.hazard: K2CO3 slurry risk — potential pump blockage
safety_flags.mitigation: Use 0.5 µm inline frit; ensure K2CO3 is fully dissolved in DMF/H2O mixture before pumping (heat gently to 40 °C if needed, then cool to RT). Alternatively switch to Cs2CO3 (more soluble in DMF) or aqueous K3PO4.

safety_flags.hazard: Pd black formation — potential reactor fouling
safety_flags.mitigation: Degas solvents rigorously. Use stabilized Pd catalyst (dppf or PPh3 ligand). Flush reactor with DMF after each run. Monitor pressure drop as fouling indicator.

safety_flags.hazard: DMF at 80 °C — potential for decomposition to dimethylamine + CO if overheated
safety_flags.mitigation: Temperature controlled and monitored with thermocouple. High-temperature alarm set at 100 °C. BPR prevents flash evaporation.

confidence.notes: High confidence in hardware design and safety controls. Yield prediction is based on literature analogies; actual yield depends on specific aryl bromide and boronic acid electronic/steric properties not specified in the batch protocol. Temperature compensation from 50 °C microwave to 80 °C thermal is an assumption based on general microwave-to-flow translation literature; experimental optimization of temperature (60–100 °C) and residence time (5–15 min) is recommended. K2CO3 solubility in DMF is a practical concern flagged but manageable.
